$comment: Hi on Fansly by the client's proof of the conversation's start (chat-extension Project Unite R20, HF-5): one fixture matrix for the hub and its client.

The hub (tests/ai-hi-start-proof.test.ts) holds its body schema to `proofs`, its request-shape rules to `shapeCases` and its gate to `gateCases`. The client's fake hub (chat-extension P6c2) copies this file VERBATIM and is held to the same answers; a change here is a change of the contract both sides read (docs/ai-gateway-contract.md, "Hi on Fansly").

`proofs`: bodies of `startProof` the schema accepts and refuses. They are the client's own fixtures (chat-extension packages/contracts/test/fixtures/fansly.ts, START_PROOF_FIXTURES): both schemas accept and refuse the same bodies.

`shapeCases`: where the three body fields (`startProof`, `personalMessageCount`, `fanAvatarUrl`) may be sent. `clientContext`: the request carries one; `capabilities`: the tokens of `x-kernel-ai-capabilities`; `fields`: the fields the body carries; `refusal`: null when the request passes these rules, else the `reason` of the 400 `bad_request`.

`gateCases`: the gate of a request on the lane (`hi-greeting`, a Fansly page, no `clientContext`, `hi-start-proof-v1` advertised). `proof`: the body's `startProof`, null when it sent none; `window`: the ids of the body's `coverageCheck.window`; `knownLiveIds`: the messages of the conversation the hub holds as not deleted; `verdict`: null when Hi is admitted, else the `reason` of the 400 `gate_hi_greeting_limit`. The first that holds: `history_unproven` without a proof; `history_unproven` when the window or the hub's live history names a message older than `startWitnessId` (any message at all when it is null); `too_many_personal` when `personalCount` is above 10.
Ids order as snowflakes: the shorter is the older, then the string order.
